div.head: Becwæð 3
div.ab: ⁊: ic agnian wylle to agenre æhte ðæt ðæt ic hæbbe ⁊ næfre ð[e m]yntan ne plot ne ploh, ne turf ne toft, ne furh ne fotmæl, ne land ne læse, ne fersc ne mersc, ne ruh ne rum, wudes ne feldes, landes ne strandes, wealtes ne wæteres;

⁊: ic agnian wille to agenre æhte þæt þæt ic hæbbe ⁊ næfre ðe myntan ne plot ne ploh, ne turf ne toft, ne furh ne fotmæl, ne land ne læsse, ne fersc ne mersc, ne ruh ne rum, wudes ne feldes, landes ne strandes, wealtes ne wæteres;

Beziehungsweise: ich will als eigen Gut behaupten, was ich habe, und niemals dir zudenken weder Fleck noch Pflug Landes, weder Rasenstück noch Hausstelle, weder Furche noch Fussbreite, weder Ackerland noch Weide, weder frisch [Wasser] noch Sumpf, weder rauhes [unebenes, buschiges?] noch offenes, an Wald noch Feld, an Land noch Strand, an Wald noch Gewässer.

Or: I will claim as my own property what I have, and never intend for you either plot or ploughland, either turf or toft, either furrow or foot's breadth, either land or pasture, either fresh [water] or marsh, either rough [uneven, bushy?] or open, of wood or field, of land or shore, of wood or water.

And I wish to own as my own property what I have, and never to devise to you [anything], plot or ploughland, turf or toft, furrow or footmark, land or meadow, fresh water or marshland, brushwood land or clearing, wood or field, land or shore, wood or water;

And I wish to own as my own property what I have, and never to devise to you [anything], plot or ploughland, turf or toft, furrow or footmark, land or meadow, fresh water or marshland, brushwood land or clearing, wood or field, land or shore, wood or water;
div.note: U: translator probably Wormald, The Making of English Law (named in the original spreadsheet’s sub-header rows): check; H reads ‘ð[e m]yntan’ (corrupt ‘ðæt yntan’); editors add ‘hit’ after ‘ic’. All editors read H's ‘wealtes’ as ‘wealdes’. B's ‘læsse’ stands so (Liebermann's text has it); B's ‘mersc’ was altered from ‘merst’. The many pairs alliterate or rhyme. Liebermann compares Swer 3.4. K: ‘læse’ corrected to B's ‘læsse’.

Nordisch. Im Testament Thurkytels (Bi 1020) Wohnstelle eines ursprünglich unfreien Kleinbauern mit Anrecht auf Stückchen Weide und Flur. Ebenso in Urkk. Bi 1014; Ke 705. ‘An einem Villan-Toft hingen später normal 2 Bovaten [¼ Hufe]’; Atkinson Cartul. Rieval. 233

Norse. In Thurkytel’s will (Bi 1020) the homestead of an originally unfree smallholder with a right to small pieces of pasture and arable. Likewise in charters Bi 1014; Ke 705. ‘To a villein’s toft there later normally belonged 2 bovates [¼ hide]’; Atkinson Cartul. Rieval. 233

‘uncleared (nor cleared), untrimmed, uncultivated’ Toller, auch s. v. rum Ia; ‘rough’ Thorpe, Cockayne; ‘rauh’ Schmid; vgl. Deutsch Raugraf ‘Graf in unbebautem Lande’; Kluge Etymol. Wb. In Glossen steht ruh für hispidus, hirsutus, pilosus, frondosus, nodosus und sein Ggs. unruh synonym mit smoeðe ‘glatt’. In Urkk. heissen ruh Berg, Hügel, Hecke, Dornicht, Sumpf. Die Eigenschaft kann also auch in der Natur, nicht bloss im Mangel an menschlichem Anbau, liegen

‘uncleared (nor cleared), untrimmed, uncultivated’ Toller, also s. v. rum Ia; ‘rough’ Thorpe, Cockayne; ‘rauh’ Schmid; cf. German Raugraf ‘count in uncultivated land’; Kluge Etymol. Wb. In glosses ruh stands for hispidus, hirsutus, pilosus, frondosus, nodosus, and its opposite unruh is synonymous with smoeðe ‘smooth’. In charters hill, mound, hedge, thorn-thicket and swamp are called ruh. The quality can thus also lie in nature, not merely in the lack of human cultivation
